title: GitLab production database deletion and restore
source_title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
alert: GitLab.com experienced a prolonged database outage during an attempted replication repair. Determine what was affected, what went wrong, and the documented recovery choice.

evidence.text: High database load caused replica WAL lag; required WAL segments had already been removed from the primary.
During replica rebuild, an engineer removed the primary data directory by mistake, deleting roughly 300 GB before stopping.
Daily pg_dump backups were missing because an incompatible PostgreSQL binary made them fail, and email alerts were rejected.
The team chose the manually created LVM snapshot from roughly six hours earlier instead of an approximately day-old alternative.
GitLab.com became unavailable; database changes to projects, comments and accounts were lost.
Git repositories and wikis were not subject to data loss, and self-managed instances were unaffected.
Copying staging data back to production took around 18 hours due to slow storage.

impact_options.name: Projects, comments and user-account updates within the lost window

root_hypotheses.description: An engineer mistakenly deleted primary PostgreSQL data while attempting to rebuild a lagging replica; backup gaps worsened recovery
An intentional attack erased all repository data
An unplanned immutable schema migration blocked inserts

response_options.description: Restore from the most recent usable six-hour-old LVM snapshot and reconstruct missing supporting data
Fail over to the already-wiped replica
Recover from the empty S3 pg_dump bucket
Disable the database permanently and delete the service

dataset_origin: Published first-party incident postmortem; curated and paraphrased source facts (NOT original telemetry)
